newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-HINGIS CONSIDERS ANOTHER HORSE RIDE AFTER FALL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS CONSIDERS ANOTHER HORSE RIDE AFTER FALL.

text.p: World number one Martina Hingis, undeterred by a riding accident last month, said on Sunday she might even go horse riding again during the French Open.
Hingis, who tore a knee ligament in the accident, said she was looking forward to her return to competitive tennis in the Paris tournament, which starts on Monday.

"I just can't wait to start playing again," the 16-year-old Swiss player said. "I was starting to miss tennis. I'm really excited to be here in Paris. This is one of my favourite tournaments and I'm certainly looking forward to it."
Smiling and looking as happy as can be, Hingis said she was even considering a horse ride with French former Olympic show jumping champion Pierre Durand.
"He invited me for next week and I said: 'Well, if I'm still in the tournament, why not?'"
Hingis also fell off her horse in January during the Australian Open in Melbourne, which she eventually won to secure her first grand slam title.
But she just laughed when somebody suggested that maybe she should stop riding.

"I've always been doing it, it's part of my life," she said. "Usually, when I'm not at home I don't fall. In Australia was the first time. But at home I do fall quite often. It's pretty good for your reactions, it makes you concentrate a little more."
Hingis, who had won all her 26 matches this season before her accident, said she felt fit and just wanted to play.
"I did undergo surgery but it was a tiny operation and I'm fine now," she said.
"It was like in a prison at home. When I arrived here three days ago I saw all the girls again and I realised I was back in a tournament. That's great.
"Me, pressure? No, why?" she asked. "I'll just go on court and play my best. If it works, it's great. If it doesn't, never mind. There will be many more tournaments to play."
Should she succeed in Paris, Hingis would not become the youngest French Open winner as Monica Seles was two months younger than Hingis is now when she won here in 1990.
But Hingis did not seem to care. Having fun seems more important to her than breaking records.
